scenes.headline: How a decision model maps a site's internal links
scenes.sub: jev-linkmap: candidate phrases, a yes-or-no judge, a gate and a cap.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Sparrow! jev-linkmap rebuilt a whole site's internal links in under six seconds. Here's how it decides where each link goes.

scenes.text: Link mapping becomes thousands of yes-or-no questions: a script with no model proposes phrases the author already wrote, and Jev only decides.
scenes.say: The trick: a plain script proposes phrases already on the page, so the model only answers yes or no. And the link lands inside a real sentence.

items.say: First, score page pairs by TF-IDF, with each page's headings counted four times.
Drop pages half the site already links to. That's menu chrome.
Keep only two-to-six-word phrases already in the page's own copy.
And mask anything already linked, so nothing is linked twice.

steps.say: Each candidate becomes a question for Jev: does this link belong, and which phrase should carry it? Eight thousand four hundred and sixty link decisions.
A rubric sets the instructions and two thresholds. Past that gate, two thousand three hundred and eighty-three yeses remain.

steps.note: a constant in a JSON file, not the judge
steps.say: Then a hard cap of three links per page, not the model, cuts that to six hundred and seventy-nine.
An editor sees one sentence per link, cuts when in doubt, and keeps two hundred and eighty-seven.

scenes.title: Recall against the referee, same holdout
scenes.note: the referee reads the same rubric it is scoring
scenes.say: A System 2 loop rewrote the rubric twice, lifting recall from forty-five to sixty-five percent. Moving just the two thresholds gets sixty-four point two.

scenes.text: The model answers yes or no; the candidates, the cap and the thresholds shape most of what ships.

recap: Candidates come from the author's own words
Thresholds, not rewrites, moved most of the recall
scenes.say: To recap: candidates from the author's words, yes or no questions, and thresholds doing most of the work.
